# Lighthouses in Wales

There are more than 30 lighthouses dotted around the Welsh coast, helping to keep sailors safe and also looking rather splendid at the same time. These are some of our favourites to visit.

SaveShare

## Trwyn Du, great for... walking

The walk out to the headland at Penmon Point, Ynys Môn (Anglesey) offers up vast views towards Puffin Island, and back across the Menai Strait to Eryri (Snowdonia). When it was built in the 1830s, [Trwyn Du lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/trwyn-du-lighthouse) featured a pioneering lavatory, which was supposed to stop seawater from surging back up the pipe. It didn’t work – which is perhaps why it has been unmanned since 1922.

![Gweld ar draws y creigiau i oleudy Trwyn Du, Ynys Môn.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__4_3_1x/public/media-library/2021-01/NVW-C57-1920-0033.jpg.webp?itok=zt9gQxxu)

Trwyn Du Lighthouse, Ynys Môn, North Wales

## South Stack, great for... location

[South Stack](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouse-visitor-centres/south-stack-lighthouse-visitor-centre) has perhaps the most spectacular setting of any Welsh lighthouse. Cross onto the island of [Ynys Môn](https://www.visitwales.com/node/4150), then hop over onto Holy Island, and finally down 400 stone steps onto yet another tiny island, where there are tours to the top of the 134ft (41m) tower. The surrounding cliffs form the [South Stack RSPB reserve](https://www.visitwales.com/product/752538) where peregrines, choughs and countless sea birds live.

![View of South Stack Lighthouse from the water.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimagegroup__portrait__1_1x/public/media-library/2018-12/N131-048-D.jpg.webp?itok=wh581wnQ)

## Llanddwyn, great for... romance

There isn’t a more romantic spot in Wales (or maybe the world…) than Llanddwyn Island. Walk out through the [Newborough Warren National Nature Reserve](https://naturalresources.wales/days-out/places-to-visit/north-west-wales/newborough/?lang=en) onto a slender, sand-fringed island, past the ruins of a chapel dedicated to [St Dwynwen](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3318/), the Welsh patron saint of lovers. And at the tip, a pair of simple whitewashed lighthouses, with breathtaking views across to Eryri.

![View looking out to sea with white lighthouse in foreground, Llanddwyn Island, North Wales](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_fullbleed__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2018-12/NVW-C104-1819-0111.jpg.webp?itok=pDTDBYhm)

Tŵr Mawr Lighthouse, Llanddwyn Island, Ynys Môn, North Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Enlli, great for... tranquility

Situated on the southern tip of [Ynys Enlli](https://www.visitwales.com/node/5297) (Bardsey Island), [Bardsey Lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/bardsey-lighthouse), the tallest square tower lighthouse in the UK, is painted in jolly red-and white bands, and its light shines red, too – it’s less dangerous for migrating birds than the old white light.

![Bardsey Island, Halbinsel Llŷn.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/NVW-C135-1819-0030.jpg.webp?itok=aXM_u0GM)

The lighthouse on Ynys Enlli, North Wales

View Credits

## Strumble Head, great for... waves

[Strumble Head Lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/strumble-head-lighthouse) sits on a small island off a rocky headland called Pencaer, or Strumble Head. This is one of Britain’s best places to spot migratory birds and passing cetaceans, and the old observation hut is popular with bird and sea watchers (the most dedicated of whom are known as ‘Strumblers’).

![Rocky and grassy headlands and sea.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2018-12/DR_Visit_Wales_Day_22944-small.jpg.webp?itok=-xqjB84B)

Strumble Head Lighthouse, Pembrokeshire, West Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Skokholm, great for... birds

Along with being home to [its lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/skokholm-lighthouse), Skokholm Island is located in a spectacular Marine Nature Reserve. It's one of the most important seabird breeding sites in the world with thousands of puffins, Manx shearwaters and storm petrels in residence. You can also take a boat trip around the island to look for birds, porpoises and dolphins. Home to similar rare marine birds and wildlife, neighbouring [Skomer Island](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3221/) is also well worth a visit and daytrips are easy to arrange.

> [View this post on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/BNkOm7JA5WJ/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

## Caldey, great for... day trips

Here’s a great day trip if you’re [holidaying in Pembrokeshire](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3053/): take the boat across from Dinbych-y-pysgod (Tenby), to [Caldey Island](https://www.visitwales.com/product/2174030), explore the Cistercian monastery, buy some homemade chocolate from the shop, and walk across the fields to the clifftop lighthouse. Together with its partner on distant Lundy Island, [Caldey Lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/caldey-island-lighthouse) guides ships into the Bristol Channel.

![Caldey Island, Pembrokeshire Coast Nationalpark.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/SVW-C30-1516-0016.jpg.webp?itok=sJq7aZr6)

Caldey Lighthouse, Pembrokeshire

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Nash Point, great for... a coastal walk

There are actually two lighthouses here on the [Glamorgan Heritage Coast’s](https://www.visitwales.com/node/3431) layer-cake cliffs, both built to warn shipping away from a treacherous sand bank. The larger was manned until 1998; now [Nash Point](https://visitthevale.com/attractions/nash-point-beach-and-lighthouse) is the only working Welsh lighthouse to have a visitor centre with a licensed wedding venue.

![A white lighthouse on a cliff edged coastline.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2019-01/SVW-C151-1818-0002-small.jpg.webp?itok=ygiBHrkE)

Nash Point, Vale of Glamorgan, South Wales

View Credits

© Hawlfraint y Goron / Crown Copyright

## Flat Holm, great for... history and nature

It’s just five miles (8km) from Caerdydd (Cardiff), but over the years [Flat Holm](https://www.visitwales.com/product/1843251) has been a saint’s retreat, a haven for pirates and smugglers, a cholera sanatorium, a gun battery, and – to stop ships bumping into it – a good place for a [lighthouse](https://www.trinityhouse.co.uk/lighthouses-and-lightvessels/flatholm-lighthouse). You can take a day trip from Caerdydd and explore the island.

![A lighthouse on a headland surrounded by the sea.](https://www.visitwales.com/sites/visit/files/styles/o_articleimage_medium__16_9_1x/public/media-library/2022-10/S132-762-D.jpg.webp?itok=qHYpZ1FN)

Flat Holm, South Wales
